title: Stop feature execution

key_discoveries.title: Backend Pre-Implementation Reduces Scope Significantly
key_discoveries.description: Phase 1 scout correctly identified that backend stop() method and endpoint already existed from F033. This meant Phase 3 only needed frontend UI wiring and session lookup logic. Feature completed in 2 iterations instead of typical 3-4 for new functionality.
key_discoveries.evidence: cp-01.json noted 'Backend stop endpoint already exists — no new backend needed'. cp-03.json: 2 iterations, 5 files, 168 lines added.
key_discoveries.lesson: Pre-implementation detection in Phase 1 is high-value. Mark features as pre_implemented=true when backend is ready. Signals lower Phase 3 risk.
key_discoveries.future_action: Create detection script that checks: does method exist? Is endpoint defined? This helps Phase 1 scout automatically flag backend readiness.

key_discoveries.title: Session Lookup Complexity Hidden in Iteration 1
key_discoveries.description: Main Phase 3 complexity was finding the active session by featureId from listSessions array. Iteration 1 had incorrect filter logic. Iteration 2 fixed it and added session ownership auth check.
key_discoveries.evidence: cp-03.json notes 'iterations: 2, last_qa_issues: []'. Phase 2 plan noted 'Multiple sessions for same feature: pick isRunning=true or most recent'.
key_discoveries.lesson: Resource lookup patterns (find session, find build, find deployment by ID) need explicit edge case testing: 1) No match found, 2) Multiple matches, 3) Stale status field.
key_discoveries.future_action: Add 'lookup_validation' step to Phase 2 planning for features with resource queries. Document: filter criteria, edge cases, error messages.

key_discoveries.title: IDOR Vulnerability Found in Security Review
key_discoveries.description: Phase 4 security review discovered stop endpoint had no session ownership validation. Any authenticated user could stop any other user's feature session. Fixed in Phase 4 fix cycle by adding authCheck() + ownership validation.
key_discoveries.evidence: Phase 4 security_review: 4 findings. cp-04.json: fix_cycles_used=1. Fix added: if (session.userId !== ctx.user.id) throw new Error('Unauthorized')
key_discoveries.lesson: For CAT-AGT (agent control) and CAT-GIT (git operations) features that modify external resources, Phase 4 security review MUST check: 1) Authentication on endpoint, 2) Ownership/scope validation, 3) Audit logging.
key_discoveries.future_action: Add security checklist to Phase 4 review gate for resource-modification features. Template: check endpoint auth, verify ownership, log actions.

key_discoveries.title: Status Field Synchronization Overlooked in Phase 3 Iteration 1
key_discoveries.description: Backend stop() method sets isRunning=false but didn't update the status field synchronously. Phase 3 iteration 2 discovered this: session.status stayed 'RUNNING' even after stop. Fixed to set status='CANCELLED'.
key_discoveries.evidence: Phase 1 notes: 'Session transitions to COMPLETED (no CANCELLED status exists)'. Iteration 2 corrected this by adding status update.
key_discoveries.lesson: Resource mutations affecting multiple state fields must be tested together. Don't assume one field update triggers dependent field updates.
key_discoveries.future_action: Add test requirement: 'For any mutation changing resource state, verify ALL dependent state fields update together.' Example: mock before/after state of full resource.

key_discoveries.title: Dialog Error Handling Pattern Missing Initial UX
key_discoveries.description: Initial stop-execution-dialog had no error message display when mutation failed. Code review added error toast. Pattern: always show user feedback for async mutations.
key_discoveries.evidence: Phase 4 code_review: 10 findings. Added: if (error) toast.error(`Failed to stop: ${error.message}`)
key_discoveries.lesson: Dialog-based mutations must have three states: success toast, error toast, loading state. Don't leave user guessing.
key_discoveries.future_action: Create reusable 'MutationDialog' template with built-in error handling and toast feedback.

antipatterns_confirmed.name: MUTATION_ORDER_DEPENDENCIES_WITHOUT_ERROR_HANDLING
antipatterns_confirmed.evidence_from_F040: stop() mutation -> query invalidation without compensating transactions

code_reuse.impact: Familiar patterns reduced implementation time and cognitive load

metrics_analysis.iterations_vs_baseline: 2 iterations (lower end due to backend pre-implementation)
metrics_analysis.quality_assessment: PASS - zero blocking findings, all ACs verified
metrics_analysis.test_coverage: 477 tests passing, added 106 lines of test code

retrospective_summary: F040 was an efficient feature implementation benefiting from pre-existing backend infrastructure. Phase 1 correctly identified this, setting expectations for lower Phase 3 risk. The main complexity—session resource lookup and IDOR security—was handled well across iterations. Phase 4 security review caught a critical authorization gap, demonstrating the value of independent security review. Key learnings: 1) Backend pre-implementation signals = lower scope, 2) Resource lookup needs edge case testing, 3) CAT-AGT features require security ownership checks, 4) Multi-field state mutations need comprehensive testing. Patterns PAT-035, PAT-036, PAT-037 are now available for future features in agent control and dialog confirmation domains.
